title.zh: 卷81 綦儁 山偉 劉仁之 宇文忠之
title.en: Volume 81: Qi Jun, Shan Wei, Liu Renzhi, Yuwen Zhongzhi
title.raw: 卷81 綦儁 山偉 劉仁之 宇文忠之 Volume 81: Qi Jun, Shan Wei, Liu Renzhi, Yuwen Zhongzhi

sentences.zh: 綦儁 山偉 劉仁之 宇文忠之

translations.literal: Qi Jun; Shan Wei; Liu Renzhi; Yuwen Zhongzhi
translations.idiomatic: Qi Jun; Shan Wei; Liu Renzhi; Yuwen Zhongzhi

sentences.zh: 綦儁，字𢶏顯，河南洛陽人也，其先代人。

translations.literal: Qi Jun, courtesy name Junxian, was a native of Luoyang in Henan; his forebears were men of Dai.
translations.idiomatic: Qi Jun, whose courtesy name was Junxian, came from Luoyang in Henan; his ancestors were northerners of Dai.

sentences.zh: 祖辰，并州刺史。

translations.literal: His grandfather Chen was governor of Bing Province.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Chen served as governor of Bing Province.

sentences.zh: 儁，莊帝時仕累遷為滄州刺史，甚為吏人畏悅。

translations.literal: Jun, serving in Emperor Zhuang's time, through successive promotions became governor of Cang Province, greatly feared and delighted in by officials and people.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Zhuang, Jun rose through successive posts to governor of Cang Province, where officials and commoners alike both feared and welcomed him.

sentences.zh: 尋除太僕卿。

translations.literal: Soon he was removed and made Grand Master of Splendid Horses.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon transferred to the post of Grand Master of Splendid Horses.

sentences.zh: 及尒朱世隆等誅，齊獻武王赴洛，止於邙山。

translations.literal: When Erzhu Shilong and the others were executed, King Xianwu of Qi went to Luoyang and halted at Mount Mang.
translations.idiomatic: After Erzhu Shilong and his faction were put to death, King Xianwu of Qi marched to Luoyang and camped at Mount Mang.

sentences.zh: 上召文武百司，下及士庶，令之曰：「尒朱暴虐，矯弄天常，孤起義信都，罪人斯翦。

translations.literal: The sovereign summoned the civil and military officials of the hundred bureaus, down to gentry and commoners, and charged them, saying: "The Erzhu were cruel and violent, perverting Heaven's constancy; I raised righteous arms at Xindu and the guilty have been cut down.
translations.idiomatic: He summoned the civil and military ranks, from high ministers down to gentry and commoners, and declared: "The Erzhu were brutal and perverted Heaven's order; I raised righteous arms at Xindu, and the guilty have been destroyed.

sentences.zh: 今將翼戴親賢，以昌魏曆，誰主社稷，允愜天人？」

translations.literal: Now I shall support and enthrone a worthy kinsman to flourish the Wei succession—who shall preside over the altars of state and satisfy both Heaven and men?"
translations.idiomatic: Now I mean to support and enthrone a worthy kinsman to revive the Wei line—who shall hold the altars of state and satisfy both Heaven and the people?"

sentences.zh: 申令頻煩，莫有應者。

translations.literal: He repeated the command again and again, but no one answered.
translations.idiomatic: He repeated the charge again and again, yet no one responded.

sentences.zh: 儁乃避席曰：「人主之體，必須度量深遠，明哲仁恕。

translations.literal: Jun then left his seat and said: "The substance of a ruler must be far-reaching in measure, wise, perspicacious, benevolent, and forgiving.
translations.idiomatic: Jun then rose from his place and said: "A ruler's character must be broad in measure, wise, clear-sighted, benevolent, and forgiving.

sentences.zh: 廣陵王遇世艱難，不言淹載，以人謀察之，雖為尒朱扶戴，[2]當今之聖主也。」

translations.literal: The Prince of Guangling met worldly hardship and, without speaking of years drowned in obscurity, judged by human counsel—though he was installed by the Erzhu[2]—he is the sage ruler of today."
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Guangling has weathered hard times; without dwelling on years spent in obscurity, judged by men's counsel—though the Erzhu set him on the throne[2]—he is the sage ruler of our day."

sentences.zh: 獻武王欣然是之。

translations.literal: King Xianwu was pleased and approved.
translations.idiomatic: King Xianwu was delighted and agreed.

sentences.zh: 時黃門侍郎崔㥄作色而前，謂儁曰：「廣陵王為主，不能紹宣魏網，[3]布德天下，為君如此，何聖之有！

translations.literal: At that time Yellow Gate Attendant Cui Lin came forward with a fierce look and said to Jun: "The Prince of Guangling as ruler could not continue and spread the Wei net,[3] extend virtue through the realm—being a lord like this, what sage is there!
translations.idiomatic: Then Yellow Gate Attendant Cui Lin stepped forward with a dark look and said to Jun: "The Prince of Guangling as ruler could not carry on and spread the Wei mandate,[3] or extend virtue through the realm—a lord like this, what sage is he!

sentences.zh: 若言其聖，應待大王。」

translations.literal: If you speak of a sage, it should await Your Highness."
translations.idiomatic: If you speak of a sage, it should be Your Highness."

sentences.zh: 時高乾邕、魏蘭根等固執 言，遂立出帝。

translations.literal: At that time Gao Ganyu, Wei Langen, and others insisted on their words, and so the fleeing emperor was enthroned.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Ganyu, Wei Langen, and others held stubbornly to their view, and so the fleeing emperor was enthroned.

sentences.zh: 及出帝失德，齊獻武王深思儁言，常以為恨。

translations.literal: When the fleeing emperor lost virtue, King Xianwu of Qi deeply pondered Jun's words and often harbored regret.
translations.idiomatic: When the fleeing emperor proved unworthy, King Xianwu of Qi often thought back on Jun's words and regretted them.

sentences.zh: 尋除御史中尉，於路與僕射賈顯度相逢，顯度恃勳貴，排儁騶列倒，儁忿見於色，自入奏之。

translations.literal: Soon he was made chief of the imperial censors; on the road he met Vice Director Jia Xiandu. Xiandu, relying on meritorious nobility, shoved Jun's outriders so their column overturned; Jun's anger showed in his face, and he entered to memorialize it himself.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon appointed chief of the imperial censors. On the road he met Vice Director Jia Xiandu, who, trusting in his noble merit, shoved aside Jun's escort until the column overturned; Jun's anger showed plainly, and he went in to report it himself.

sentences.zh: 尋加散騎常侍、驃騎大將軍、左光祿大夫、儀同三司。

translations.literal: Soon he was also given the posts of regular attendant at scattered cavalry, grand general of agile cavalry, left grand master of resplendent fortune, and bearer of ritual equal to the Three Excellencies.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon also made regular attendant at scattered cavalry, grand general of agile cavalry, left grand master of resplendent fortune, and bearer of ritual equal to the Three Excellencies.

sentences.zh: 儁佞巧，能候當塗，斛斯椿、賀拔勝皆與友善。

translations.literal: Jun was fawning and crafty, able to watch those in power; Dusi Chun and Heba Sheng were all on friendly terms with him.
translations.idiomatic: Jun was sycophantic and cunning, skilled at watching those who held power; Dusi Chun and Heba Sheng were both his friends.

sentences.zh: 斛斯椿之搆間也，出帝令儁奉詔晉陽，齊獻武王集文武與儁申釋，儁辭屈而退。

translations.literal: When Dusi Chun sowed dissension, the fleeing emperor ordered Jun to carry an edict to Jinyang; King Xianwu of Qi gathered civil and military officials to explain matters with Jun, and Jun was silenced and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: When Dusi Chun stirred up discord, the fleeing emperor sent Jun to Jinyang with an edict; King Xianwu of Qi assembled his civil and military officers to clear matters with Jun, and Jun, defeated in argument, withdrew.

sentences.zh: 性多詐。

translations.literal: His nature was full of deceit.
translations.idiomatic: He was by nature deeply deceitful.

sentences.zh: 賀拔勝出鎮荊州，過儁別，因辭儁母，儁故見敗氊弊被，勝更遺之錢物。

translations.literal: When Heba Sheng went out to command Jing Province and passed to take leave of Jun, he also paid respects to Jun's mother; Jun deliberately displayed tattered felt and worn bedding, and Sheng further sent him money and goods.
translations.idiomatic: When Heba Sheng took up command of Jing Province he called on Jun to bid farewell and also paid his respects to Jun's mother; Jun deliberately showed tattered felt and ragged bedding, and Sheng sent him still more money and goods.

sentences.zh: 後兼吏部尚書，復為滄州刺史。

translations.literal: Later he concurrently served as minister of the Ministry of Personnel and again became governor of Cang Province.
translations.idiomatic: Later he served concurrently as minister of the Ministry of Personnel and again as governor of Cang Province.

sentences.zh: 徵還，兼中尉，章武縣伯。

translations.literal: Summoned back, he concurrently held the censorate and was enfeoffed as Baron of Zhangwu county.
translations.idiomatic: Recalled to court, he again held the censorate and was enfeoffed as Baron of Zhangwu.

sentences.zh: 尋除殷州刺史，薨於州。

translations.literal: Soon he was made governor of Yin Province and died in office.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made governor of Yin Province and died there.

sentences.zh: 贈司空公，諡曰文貞。

translations.literal: Posthumously he was given the office of Duke of Works; his posthumous title was Wenzhen.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made Duke of Works, with the posthumous title Wenzhen.

sentences.zh: 子洪寔，字巨正。

translations.literal: His son Hongshi, courtesy name Juzheng.
translations.idiomatic: His son Hongshi, courtesy name Juzheng.

sentences.zh: 位尚書左右郎，魏郡邑中正。

translations.literal: He held the posts of left and right gentlemen of the Masters of Writing and district eligibility director for Wei commandery.
translations.idiomatic: He served as left and right gentleman of the Masters of Writing and as district eligibility director for Wei commandery.

sentences.zh: 嗜酒好色，無行檢。

translations.literal: He was addicted to wine and lust, without conduct or restraint.
translations.idiomatic: He was addicted to wine and women and utterly without moral restraint.

sentences.zh: 卒官。

translations.literal: He died in office.
translations.idiomatic: He died in office.

sentences.zh: 山偉，字仲才，河南洛陽人也，其先代人。

translations.literal: Shan Wei, courtesy name Zhongcai, was a native of Luoyang in Henan; his forebears were men of Dai.
translations.idiomatic: Shan Wei, courtesy name Zhongcai, came from Luoyang in Henan; his ancestors were northerners of Dai.

sentences.zh: 祖強，美容貌，身長八尺五寸，工騎射，彎弓五石。

translations.literal: His grandfather Qiang had a handsome face, stood eight chi five cun tall, was skilled at mounted archery, and could draw a bow of five shi.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Qiang was handsome, stood eight feet five inches tall, excelled at mounted archery, and could draw a bow rated at five shi.

sentences.zh: 為奏事中散，從顯祖獵方山，有兩狐起於御前，詔強射之，百步內二狐俱獲。

translations.literal: He served as palace attendant among those who presented memorials; following Emperor Xianzu on a hunt at Mount Fang, two foxes sprang up before the imperial carriage, and an edict ordered Qiang to shoot; within a hundred paces both foxes were taken.
translations.idiomatic: As a memorial-presenting palace attendant, he followed Emperor Xianzu hunting at Mount Fang; two foxes broke cover before the imperial carriage, and the emperor ordered Qiang to shoot—within a hundred paces he took both.

sentences.zh: 位內行長。

translations.literal: He held the post of chief of inner conduct.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to chief of inner conduct.

sentences.zh: 父稚之，營陵令。

translations.literal: His father Zhizhi was magistrate of Yingling.
translations.idiomatic: His father Zhizhi served as magistrate of Yingling.

sentences.zh: 偉隨父之縣，遂師事縣人王惠，涉獵文史。

translations.literal: Wei accompanied his father to the county and there took Wang Hui of the district as his teacher, ranging widely through belles-lettres and history.
translations.idiomatic: Wei went with his father to the county and took Wang Hui, a local scholar, as his teacher, reading widely in literature and history.

sentences.zh: 稚之位金明太守。

translations.literal: Zhizhi rose to governor of Jinming.
translations.idiomatic: Zhizhi later became governor of Jinming.

sentences.zh: 肅宗初，元匡為御史中尉，以偉兼侍御史。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Emperor Suzong's reign, Yuan Kuang was chief of the censors and had Wei serve concurrently as attendant censor.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Emperor Suzong's reign Yuan Kuang was chief of the censors and appointed Wei as concurrent attendant censor.

sentences.zh: 入臺五日，便遇正會。

translations.literal: Five days after entering the bureau he encountered a great court session.
translations.idiomatic: Five days after entering the censorate he attended a full court assembly.

sentences.zh: 偉司神武門，其妻從叔為羽林隊主，撾直長於殿門，偉即劾奏。

translations.literal: Wei was in charge of the Divine Martial Gate; his wife's cousin served as leader of the feathered guard and struck a straight officer at the palace gate, and Wei immediately impeached and reported it.
translations.idiomatic: Wei was stationed at the Divine Martial Gate; his wife's cousin, a leader of the feathered guard, beat a straight officer at the palace gate, and Wei at once impeached him.

sentences.zh: 匡善之，俄然奏正。

translations.literal: Kuang approved; before long he was submitted for regular appointment.
translations.idiomatic: Kuang commended him, and before long he was promoted to a regular post.

sentences.zh: 帖國子助教，遷員外郎、廷尉評。

translations.literal: He was posted as assistant tutor in the National University, then transferred to outside-section gentleman and assessor in the Court of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: He was assigned as assistant tutor at the National University, then moved to outside-section gentleman and assessor in the Court of Justice.

sentences.zh: 時天下無事，進仕路難，代遷之人，多不霑預。

translations.literal: At that time the realm was at peace and the road to advancement was difficult; men transferred from Dai in their generation were mostly not included.
translations.idiomatic: The realm was then at peace and advancement was hard; northerners of the Dai generation were largely passed over.

sentences.zh: 及六鎮、隴西二方起逆，領軍元叉欲用代來寒人為傳詔以慰悅之，而牧守子孫投狀求者百餘人。

translations.literal: When the six garrisons and the two regions of Longxi rose in revolt, the army supervisor Yuan Cha wished to use northerners newly come from Dai as edict-bearers to soothe and please them, while sons and grandsons of governors and defenders submitted petitions seeking appointment—more than a hundred men.
translations.idiomatic: When the six garrisons and Longxi rebelled, army supervisor Yuan Cha wished to appoint newly arrived northerners from Dai as edict-bearers to win them over, yet more than a hundred sons and grandsons of governors and defenders submitted petitions seeking posts.

sentences.zh: 又欲杜之，因奏立勳附隊，令各依資出身。

translations.literal: Cha also wished to stop this and therefore memorialized to establish an attached merit corps, directing each to enter office according to qualifications.
translations.idiomatic: Cha also wished to block this and memorialized to establish an attached merit corps, ordering each man to enter office according to his qualifications.

sentences.zh: 自是北人悉被收敍。

translations.literal: From then on northerners were all enrolled.
translations.idiomatic: From then on northerners were all given appointments.

sentences.zh: 偉遂奏記，贊叉德美。

translations.literal: Wei then submitted a note praising Cha's virtue and beauty.
translations.idiomatic: Wei then sent in a memorial praising Cha's virtue.

sentences.zh: 叉素不識偉，訪侍中安豐王延明、黃門郎元順，順等因是稱薦之。

translations.literal: Cha had never known Wei; he inquired of Palace Attendant Prince Anfeng Wang Yanming and yellow gate gentleman Yuan Shun, and Shun and the others thereupon praised and recommended him.
translations.idiomatic: Cha had never known Wei and asked Palace Attendant Prince Anfeng, Yanming, and yellow gate gentleman Yuan Shun; Shun and the others thereupon recommended him.

sentences.zh: 叉令僕射元欽引偉兼尚書二千石郎，後正名士郎。

translations.literal: Cha had Vice Director Yuan Qin bring Wei in as concurrent gentleman of two thousand piculs in the Masters of Writing, later made regular gentleman of famous scholars.
translations.idiomatic: Cha had Vice Director Yuan Qin bring Wei in as concurrent gentleman of two thousand piculs in the Masters of Writing; later he was made regular gentleman of famous scholars.

sentences.zh: [4]修起居注。

translations.literal: [4] He revised the imperial diary.
translations.idiomatic: [4] He worked on the imperial diary.

sentences.zh: 僕射元順領選，表薦為諫議大夫。

translations.literal: Vice Director Yuan Shun oversaw selection and on memorial recommended him as remonstrator and adviser.
translations.idiomatic: Vice Director Yuan Shun, who oversaw selection, memorialized recommending him as remonstrator and adviser.

sentences.zh: 尒朱榮之害朝士，偉時守直，故免禍。

translations.literal: When Erzhu Rong killed court gentlemen, Wei was then on straight duty and therefore escaped disaster.
translations.idiomatic: When Erzhu Rong slaughtered court officials, Wei happened to be on straight duty and so escaped harm.

sentences.zh: 及莊帝入宮，仍除偉給事黃門侍郎。

translations.literal: When Emperor Zhuang entered the palace, Wei was still made gentleman attendant at the yellow gate.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Zhuang took the palace, Wei was made gentleman attendant at the yellow gate.

sentences.zh: 先是，偉與儀曹郎袁昇、屯田郎李延孝、外兵郎李奐、三公郎王延業方駕而行，偉少居後。

translations.literal: Earlier, Wei had been riding abreast with Ritual Director Yuan Sheng, Field Director Li Yanxiao, External Troops Director Li Huan, and Three Ducal Houses Director Wang Yanye—Wei, being younger, lagged behind.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Wei had been riding with Ritual Director Yuan Sheng, Field Director Li Yanxiao, External Troops Director Li Huan, and Three Ducal Houses Director Wang Yanye; Wei, being the youngest, trailed behind.

sentences.zh: 路逢一尼，望之歎曰：「此輩緣業，同日而死。」

translations.literal: On the road they met a nun, who looked at them and sighed: "This group's karmic lot is to die on the same day."
translations.idiomatic: On the road they met a nun who looked at them and sighed: "These men's karmic lot binds them to die on the same day."

sentences.zh: 謂偉曰：「君方近天子，當作好官。」

translations.literal: She said to Wei: "You will soon be near the Son of Heaven—take a good office."
translations.idiomatic: She said to Wei: "You are about to draw near the Son of Heaven—you will hold a fine office."

sentences.zh: 而昇等四人，皆於河陰遇害，果如其言。

translations.literal: Sheng and the other four all met their end at Heyin, exactly as she had said.
translations.idiomatic: Sheng and the other four were all killed at Heyin, exactly as she had foretold.

sentences.zh: 俄領著作郎。

translations.literal: Before long he headed the Bureau of Compilation.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he headed the Bureau of Compilation.

sentences.zh: 前廢帝立，除安東將軍、祕書監，仍著作。

translations.literal: When the Deposed Emperor of Former times was enthroned, he was made general who pacifies the east and supervisor of the secretariat, while still compiling.
translations.idiomatic: When the former Deposed Emperor was enthroned, he was made general who pacifies the east and supervisor of the secretariat while still heading compilation.

sentences.zh: 初，尒朱兆之入洛，官守奔散，國史典書高法顯密埋史書，故不遺落。

translations.literal: At first, when Erzhu Zhao entered Luoyang, guards of office scattered in flight; the state historian and keeper of canon Gao Faxian secretly buried the historical writings, so nothing was lost.
translations.idiomatic: When Erzhu Zhao first entered Luoyang, officials fled in disorder; state historian and keeper of the canon Gao Faxian secretly buried the historical records, so nothing was lost.

sentences.zh: 偉自以為功，訴求爵賞。

translations.literal: Wei took this as his own merit and petitioned for rank and reward.
translations.idiomatic: Wei claimed the credit for himself and petitioned for rank and reward.

sentences.zh: 偉挾附世隆，遂封東阿縣伯，而法顯止獲男爵。

translations.literal: Wei leaned on Shilong's favor and was enfeoffed Baron of Dong'e, while Faxian received only a male noble rank.
translations.idiomatic: Wei relied on Shilong's patronage and was enfeoffed Baron of Dong'e, while Faxian received only a baron's rank.

sentences.zh: 偉尋進侍中。

translations.literal: Wei was soon advanced to palace attendant.
translations.idiomatic: Wei was soon promoted to palace attendant.

sentences.zh: 孝靜初，除衞大將軍、中書令、監起居。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Emperor Xiaojing, he was made grand general of the guard, director of the secretariat, and overseer of the imperial diary.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Emperor Xiaojing's reign he was made grand general of the guard, director of the secretariat, and overseer of the imperial diary.

sentences.zh: 後以本官復領著作，卒官。

translations.literal: Later, in that same office, he again headed compilation and died in office.
translations.idiomatic: Later, while still holding those posts, he again headed compilation and died in office.

sentences.zh: 贈驃騎大將軍、開府儀同三司、都督、幽州刺史，諡曰文貞公。

translations.literal: Posthumously he was given grand general of agile cavalry, open bureau with ritual equal to the Three Excellencies, area commander, governor of You Province; his posthumous title was Duke Wenzhen.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made grand general of agile cavalry, bearer of the open bureau with ritual equal to the Three Excellencies, area commander, and governor of You Province, with the posthumous title Duke Wenzhen.

sentences.zh: 國史自鄧淵、崔琛、崔浩、高允、李彪、崔光以還，諸人相繼撰錄，綦儁及偉等諂說上黨王天穆及尒朱世隆，以為國書正應代人修緝，不宜委之餘人，是以儁、偉等更主大籍。

translations.literal: The national histories, from Deng Yuan, Cui Chen, Cui Hao, Gao Yun, Li Biao, Cui Guang onward, were written in succession by various men; Qi Jun and Wei and others flattered Shangdang Wang Tianmu and Erzhu Shilong, saying that the national book ought properly to be compiled by men of Dai and should not be entrusted to others—thus Jun, Wei, and the others again took charge of the great registers.
translations.idiomatic: Since Deng Yuan, Cui Chen, Cui Hao, Gao Yun, Li Biao, and Cui Guang, the national history had been compiled in turn by successive scholars; Qi Jun, Wei, and others flattered Shangdang Prince Tianmu and Erzhu Shilong, arguing that the state annals ought to be edited by men of Dai and not entrusted to outsiders—so Jun, Wei, and their circle again took charge of the great registers.

sentences.zh: 守舊而已，初無述著。

translations.literal: They only guarded the old and at first did no composing or setting forth.
translations.idiomatic: They merely preserved what was already there and produced nothing new.

sentences.zh: 故自崔鴻死後，迄終偉身，二十許載，時事蕩然，萬不記一，後人執筆，無所憑據，史之遺闕，偉之由也。

translations.literal: Thus from after Cui Hong's death until Wei's own end—some twenty years—the affairs of the time were in turmoil and ten thousand parts in ten thousand were unrecorded; when men later took up the brush they had nothing to rely on; the lacunae in history were owing to Wei.
translations.idiomatic: From Cui Hong's death until Wei's own end—roughly twenty years—the events of the age were left in chaos; scarcely one in ten thousand was recorded, and later historians had nothing to work from. The gaps in the history were Wei's doing.

sentences.zh: 外示沉厚，內實矯競。

translations.literal: Outwardly he showed depth and weight; inwardly he was in fact aggressively contentious.
translations.idiomatic: Outwardly he seemed grave and steady; inwardly he was fiercely competitive.

sentences.zh: 與綦儁少甚相得，晚以名位之間，遂若水火。

translations.literal: With Qi Jun he was on very good terms in youth; in later years, over questions of name and rank, they became like fire and water.
translations.idiomatic: He and Qi Jun were close in youth; in later years, over rank and standing, they became like fire and water.

sentences.zh: 與宇文忠之之徒、代人為黨，時賢畏惡之。

translations.literal: With Yuwen Zhongzhi's crowd he formed a clique of men of Dai; men of the time feared and detested them.
translations.idiomatic: He formed a faction with Yuwen Zhongzhi and other men of Dai; the worthies of the day feared and despised them.

sentences.zh: 而愛尚文史，老而彌篤。

translations.literal: Yet he loved and valued belles-lettres and history, growing more ardent in old age.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he loved literature and history, and grew only more devoted in old age.

sentences.zh: 偉弟少亡，偉撫寡訓孤，同居二十餘載，恩義甚篤。

translations.literal: Wei's younger brother died young; Wei nurtured the widow and taught the orphan, living together more than twenty years in very earnest kindness.
translations.idiomatic: Wei's younger brother died young; Wei raised the widow and taught the orphan, and they lived together more than twenty years in deep affection.

sentences.zh: 不營產業，身亡之後，賣宅營葬，妻子不免飄泊，士友歎愍之。

translations.literal: He did not manage property; after his death his house was sold to arrange burial, and wife and children could not escape drifting destitution—scholar-officials sighed and pitied them.
translations.idiomatic: He never built up an estate; after his death his house was sold to pay for burial, and his wife and children were left adrift—scholar-officials mourned them.

sentences.zh: 長子昂襲爵。

translations.literal: His eldest son Ang inherited the title.
translations.idiomatic: His eldest son Ang inherited the title.

sentences.zh: 劉仁之，字山靜，河南洛陽人。

translations.literal: Liu Renzhi, courtesy name Shanjing, was a man of Luoyang in Henan.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Renzhi, courtesy name Shanjing, was from Luoyang in Henan.

sentences.zh: 其先代人，徙于洛。

translations.literal: His forebears were men of Dai who moved to Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: His ancestors were northerners of Dai who had moved to Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 父爾頭，在外戚傳。

translations.literal: His father Er'tou is in the biographies of consorts' kin.
translations.idiomatic: His father Er'tou is treated in the biographies of consorts' kin.

sentences.zh: 仁之少有操尚，粗涉書史，真草書迹，頗號工便。

translations.literal: Renzhi in youth had moral resolve, roughly ranged through books and histories, and in regular and cursive script his traces were famed as quite handy.
translations.idiomatic: Renzhi in youth had moral resolve, read broadly in books and histories, and was known as skilled in both regular and cursive script.

sentences.zh: 御史中尉元昭引為御史。

translations.literal: Chief of censors Yuan Zhao brought him in as censor.
translations.idiomatic: Chief of censors Yuan Zhao brought him in as a censor.

sentences.zh: 前廢帝時，兼黃門侍郎，深為尒朱世隆所信用。

translations.literal: In the time of the Deposed Emperor of Former times he concurrently served as gentleman of the yellow gate and was deeply trusted by Erzhu Shilong.
translations.idiomatic: Under the former Deposed Emperor he served concurrently as gentleman of the yellow gate and was deeply trusted by Erzhu Shilong.

sentences.zh: 出帝初，為著作郎，兼中書令，既非其才，在史未嘗執筆。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the fleeing emperor he was made compilation gentleman and concurrently director of the secretariat; it was not his talent, and in the history bureau he never took up the brush.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of the fleeing emperor's reign he was made compilation gentleman and concurrently director of the secretariat; the post was beyond his ability, and in the history office he never actually wrote.

sentences.zh: 出除衞將軍、西兗州刺史，在州有當時之譽。

translations.literal: He went out and was made general of the guard and governor of Western Yan Province; in the province he had a reputation of the day.
translations.idiomatic: He left court to serve as general of the guard and governor of Western Yan Province, where he won a fine reputation.

sentences.zh: 武定二年卒，贈衞大將軍、吏部尚書、青州刺史，諡曰敬。

translations.literal: In the second year of Wuding he died; posthumously he was given grand general of the guard, minister of the Ministry of Personnel, governor of Qing Province; his posthumous title was Jing.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the second year of Wuding and was posthumously made grand general of the guard, minister of the Ministry of Personnel, and governor of Qing Province, with the posthumous title Jing.

sentences.zh: 仁之外示長者，內懷矯詐。

translations.literal: Outwardly Renzhi displayed the bearing of an elder; inwardly he harbored deceit and craft.
translations.idiomatic: Outwardly Renzhi played the elder; inwardly he was full of deceit.

sentences.zh: 其對賓客，破牀弊席，粗飯冷菜，衣服故敗，乃過逼下。

translations.literal: Toward guests he broke beds and worn mats, coarse rice and cold dishes, clothes old and ruined—thus he overpressed those below.
translations.idiomatic: With guests he offered broken beds and ragged mats, coarse rice and cold dishes, and worn-out clothes—going to excess to humble himself.

sentences.zh: 善候當途，能為詭激。

translations.literal: He was skilled at watching those in power and could perform abrupt provocations.
translations.idiomatic: He was skilled at watching those in power and could stage sudden dramatic gestures.

sentences.zh: 每於稠人廣眾之中，或撾一姦吏，或縱一孤貧，大言自眩，示己高明，矜物無知。

translations.literal: Whenever in a dense crowd or broad assembly he would sometimes beat a corrupt official or sometimes release a lone poor man, speaking loudly to dazzle others, showing himself lofty and bright, condescending that things were ignorant of him.
translations.idiomatic: In crowded public gatherings he would sometimes beat a corrupt official or sometimes release a lone poor man, declaiming loudly to dazzle others, showing himself lofty and looking down on the ignorant world.

sentences.zh: 淺識皆稱其美，公能之譽，動過其實。

translations.literal: Men of shallow insight all praised his beauty; the reputation of public talent exceeded the fact.
translations.idiomatic: Shallow observers all praised him; his reputation for public virtue far outran the reality.

sentences.zh: 性又酷虐，在晉陽曾營城雉，仁之統監作役，以小稽緩，遂杖前殷州刺史裴瑗、并州刺史王綽，齊獻武王大加譴責。

translations.literal: His nature was also cruel and violent; at Jinyang he once oversaw city walls; Renzhi directed and supervised the labor, and for a small delay in pace he had the former Yin Province governor Pei Yuan and Bing Province governor Wang Chuo beaten—King Xianwu of Qi greatly denounced him.
translations.idiomatic: He was also cruel by nature. At Jinyang, when city walls were under construction, Renzhi supervised the labor; for a slight delay he had the former governor of Yin Province, Pei Yuan, and the governor of Bing Province, Wang Chuo, beaten—King Xianwu of Qi rebuked him severely.

sentences.zh: 性好文字，吏書失體，便加鞭撻，言韻微訛，亦見捶楚，吏民苦之。

translations.literal: He loved written forms; if clerical documents lost proper form he would add the whip; if pronunciation or rhyme was slightly wrong he also saw the cudgel—clerks and people suffered.
translations.idiomatic: He was exacting about written forms; if a clerk's document was improperly formatted he would flog him, and if a word's pronunciation or tone was slightly off he would beat him as well—officials and commoners alike suffered under him.

sentences.zh: 而愛好文史，敬重人流。

translations.literal: Yet he loved belles-lettres and history and respected men of culture.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he loved literature and history and treated men of letters with respect.

sentences.zh: 與齋帥馮元興交款，元興死後積年，仁之營視其家，常出隆厚。

translations.literal: He was on close terms with director of auspices Feng Yuanxing; years after Yuanxing's death Renzhi still managed and watched his household, often giving generously.
translations.idiomatic: He was close to director of auspices Feng Yuanxing; years after Yuanxing's death Renzhi still looked after his household and often gave generously.

sentences.zh: 時人以此尚之。

translations.literal: Men of the time for this held him in esteem.
translations.idiomatic: Men of the time esteemed him for this.

sentences.zh: 字文忠之，河南洛陽人也。

translations.literal: Yuwen Zhongzhi was a native of Luoyang in Henan.
translations.idiomatic: Yuwen Zhongzhi was from Luoyang in Henan.

sentences.zh: 其先南單于之遠屬，世據東部，後入居代都。

translations.literal: His forebears were distant kin of the southern Chanyu; for generations they held the eastern regions, later entering to dwell at the Dai capital.
translations.idiomatic: His ancestors were distant kin of the southern Chanyu; for generations they held the eastern territories, later settling at the Dai capital.

sentences.zh: 祖阿生，安南將軍，巴西公。

translations.literal: His grandfather Asheng was general who pacifies the south and Duke of Brazil.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Asheng was general who pacifies the south and Duke of Brazil.

sentences.zh: 父侃，卒於治書侍御史。

translations.literal: His father Kan died while serving as attendant at the editorial court.
translations.idiomatic: His father Kan died while serving as editorial court attendant.

sentences.zh: 忠之獵涉文史，頗有筆札，釋褐太學博士。

translations.literal: Zhongzhi ranged through belles-lettres and history, had considerable brushwork, and on leaving the sackcloth was made erudite of the Imperial University.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongzhi read widely in literature and history, wrote competently, and on entering office was made erudite of the Imperial University.

sentences.zh: 天平初，除中書侍郎。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tianping, he was made attendant of the secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of the Tianping era he was made attendant of the secretariat.

sentences.zh: 裴伯茂與之同省，常侮忽之，以忠之色黑，呼為「黑宇」。

translations.literal: Pei Bomao was in the same bureau with him and often treated him with contempt; because Zhong was dark in complexion, he called him "Black Yu."
translations.idiomatic: Pei Bomao served in the same bureau and often slighted him; because Zhongzhi was dark-skinned, he nicknamed him "Black Yu."

sentences.zh: 後敕修國史。

translations.literal: Later he was ordered to revise the national history.
translations.idiomatic: Later he received orders to compile the national history.

sentences.zh: 元象初，兼通直散騎常侍，副鄭伯猷使蕭衍。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Yuanxiang, he concurrently served as regular attendant of direct communication at scattered cavalry and accompanied Zheng Boyou on a mission to Xiao Yan.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of the Yuanxiang era he served concurrently as regular attendant of direct communication at scattered cavalry and accompanied Zheng Boyou on a mission to Xiao Yan.

sentences.zh: 武定初，為安南將軍、尚書右丞，仍修史。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Wuding, he was made general who pacifies the south and right vice director of the Masters of Writing, while still revising history.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Wuding he was made general who pacifies the south and right vice director of the Masters of Writing while still compiling history.

sentences.zh: 未幾，以事除名。

translations.literal: Before long, because of an affair he was stripped of name and rank.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was dismissed and stripped of rank because of an offense.

sentences.zh: 忠之好榮利，自為中書郎，六七年矣，遇尚書省選右丞，預選者皆射策，忠之入試焉。

translations.literal: Zhongzhi loved glory and profit; since becoming attendant of the secretariat six or seven years had passed, when the Masters of Writing bureau selected a right vice director—all candidates shot arrows at targets in examination—and Zhongzhi entered the test.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongzhi loved rank and profit; he had been an attendant of the secretariat for six or seven years when the Masters of Writing selected a right vice director—all candidates took the archery examination—and Zhongzhi entered the competition.

sentences.zh: 既獲丞職，大為忻滿，志氣囂然，有驕物之色，識者笑之。

translations.literal: Having obtained the vice director post, he was greatly pleased and satisfied, his spirit arrogant, with a look that despised things—those who knew him laughed.
translations.idiomatic: Once he won the vice director post he was elated, swaggering with arrogant airs and a look that scorned others—those who knew him laughed.

sentences.zh: 既失官爵，怏怏發病卒。

translations.literal: Having lost office and rank, he died resentfully of illness.
translations.idiomatic: After losing his office and rank he fell ill with resentment and died.

sentences.zh: 子君山。

translations.literal: His son Junshan.
translations.idiomatic: His son Junshan.

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：綦儁遭逢受職；

translations.literal: The historian says: Qi Jun encountered fortune and received office;
translations.idiomatic: The historian writes: Qi Jun met with opportunity and took office;

sentences.zh: 山偉位行頗爽；

translations.literal: Shan Wei's position and conduct were rather upright;
translations.idiomatic: Shan Wei's rank and conduct were fairly upright;

sentences.zh: 仁之雖內懷矯詐，而交情自篤；

translations.literal: Renzhi, though inwardly harboring deceit and craft, was earnest in friendship;
translations.idiomatic: Renzhi, though inwardly deceitful, was steadfast in friendship;

sentences.zh: 忠之雖文史足用，而雅道蔑聞。

translations.literal: Zhongzhi, though sufficient in belles-lettres and history, showed no refinement of manner.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongzhi, though competent in letters and history, showed no trace of refined conduct.

sentences.zh: 謂全德者，其難矣哉！

translations.literal: To call any of them fully virtuous—how difficult!
translations.idiomatic: To call any of them wholly virtuous—how difficult indeed!

sentences.zh: 校勘記

translations.literal: Collation notes
translations.idiomatic: Textual notes

sentences.zh: 魏書卷八十一 諸本目錄此卷注「闕」。

translations.literal: Wei shu juan 81: In the tables of contents of various editions this juan is marked "deficient."
translations.idiomatic: Wei shu juan 81: In the tables of contents of various editions this scroll is marked "lacunose."

sentences.zh: 殿本考證云：「魏收書闕，後人所補。」

translations.literal: The Palace Edition textual verification says: "Wei Shou's text is missing; later persons supplemented it."
translations.idiomatic: The Palace Edition notes: "Wei Shou's text is missing; later hands supplied this."

sentences.zh: 按此卷以北史卷五０綦儁、山偉、宇文忠之三傳及卷二０劉庫仁附劉仁之傳補。

translations.literal: According to this, this juan was supplemented from Beishi juan 50 biographies of Qi Jun, Shan Wei, and Yuwen Zhongzhi and juan 20 Liu Kuren appendix Liu Renzhi biography.
translations.idiomatic: This scroll was patched from Beishi juan 50 (biographies of Qi Jun, Shan Wei, and Yuwen Zhongzhi) and juan 20 (Liu Kuren appendix, Liu Renzhi).

sentences.zh: 卷末無宋人校語，當是脫去。

translations.literal: At the end of the juan there are no Song-dynasty collation notes; they must have been lost.
translations.idiomatic: The scroll ends without Song-dynasty collation notes; they must have dropped out.

sentences.zh: 雖為尒朱扶戴 諸本「戴」訛「載」，今據北史卷五０綦儁傳改。

translations.literal: Though installed by the Erzhu — In various editions "dai" (install) is written erroneously as "zai" (carry/load); now emended according to Beishi juan 50 Qi Jun biography.
translations.idiomatic: "Though installed by the Erzhu": editions wrongly read dai (install) as zai (carry); emended per Beishi juan 50, Qi Jun biography.

sentences.zh: 不能紹宣魏網 按文義「網」當是「綱」之訛。

translations.literal: Could not continue and spread the Wei net — According to the sense, "wang" (net) should be the error for "gang" (great principle).
translations.idiomatic: "Could not continue and spread the Wei mandate": by sense wang (net) should read gang (cord/principle).

sentences.zh: 後正名士郎 張森楷云：「『名士』二字疑誤。」

translations.literal: Later made regular gentleman of famous scholars — Zhang Senkai says: "The two characters 'ming shi' (famous scholars) are suspected to be in error."
translations.idiomatic: "Later made regular gentleman of famous scholars": Zhang Senkai says, "The two characters mingshi (famous scholars) are probably wrong."

sentences.zh: 按墓誌集釋元湛墓誌

translations.literal: According to Jishi jishi, Yuan Zhan muzhiming (epitaph of Yuan Zhan)
translations.idiomatic: Per Jishi jishi, epitaph of Yuan Zhan

sentences.zh: 〈圖版一五二〉

translations.literal: 〈Plate 152〉
translations.idiomatic: 〈Plate 152〉

sentences.zh: 稱「尋補尚書左士郎中」，周書卷三四楊敷傳稱敷「歷尚書左士郎中」。

translations.literal: It says "soon supplemented as gentleman of left scholar in the Masters of Writing"; Zhou shu juan 34 Yang Fu biography says Fu "passed through gentleman of left scholar in the Masters of Writing."
translations.idiomatic: it reads "soon supplemented as gentleman of the left scholar office in the Masters of Writing"; Zhou shu juan 34, Yang Fu biography, says Fu "served as gentleman of the left scholar office in the Masters of Writing."

sentences.zh: 左右士曹見晉書卷二四職官志。

translations.literal: The left and right scholar offices are in Jin shu juan 24 Offices treatise.
translations.idiomatic: The left and right scholar offices appear in Jin shu juan 24, Treatise on Offices.

sentences.zh: 疑這裏「名」字乃「右」字之訛。

translations.literal: It is suspected that here the character "ming" (name/famous) is the error for "you" (left).
translations.idiomatic: Here ming (famous) is probably a corruption of you (left).
